evidence: Each job card on homepage shows title, company, location, salary range, date, industry/type tags, and skills (e.g. "Senior Frontend Developer", "San Francisco, CA", "$140k - $180k").
Homepage lists "Showing 8 jobs" with 8 job cards visible covering multiple industries/types.
Industry filter (Technology → 2 jobs), Location filter (Remote → 2 jobs), Job Type filter (Contract → 1 job) all correctly narrowed results.
Searching "Python" correctly returned only "Data Analyst" job which has Python as a skill.
All filter/search changes (industry, location, job type, keyword) updated the "Showing N jobs" count and list instantly without page reload.
Job details page for job-1 shows full description, responsibilities, requirements, and required skills tags (React, TypeScript, CSS, Node.js).

Application form fields (Full Name, Email, Cover Letter) are HTML5-required and blocked submission when empty (checkValidity=false). Email field also rejected invalid format "not-an-email" (type=email, checkValidity=false).
Filled Full Name, Email, Cover Letter/Message and submitted successfully; confirmation toast "Application submitted!" appeared and form reset.
Submission returned a success notification without errors: "Your application for Senior Frontend Developer at TechCorp Solutions has been sent."

actual: Submitted a second application to the same job (job-1) using the identical name "Jane Test" and email "jane.test@example.com" as a prior successful submission. The system accepted it and displayed "Application submitted! Your application for Senior Frontend Developer at TechCorp Solutions has been sent." with no warning or rejection of the duplicate.

issue: Incomplete job posting was published without required fields
actual: Submitted a job with only Title, Description, Min/Max Salary filled — Industry, Employment Type, and Location dropdowns were left at their default unselected placeholder state. Instead of being blocked, the job was published successfully ("Job posted successfully! Your job listing is now live and visible to job seekers.") and now appears in the dashboard as "Test Job" with missing location/industry/type info (listing shows "· $50k - $70k · Posted Yesterday" with no location, no industry/type tags).

evidence: Employer dashboard "Your Job Listings" section lists all 5 posted jobs (Senior Frontend Developer, Product Designer, Marketing Manager, Part-Time Content Writer, DevOps Engineer) with Active Jobs count.

Clicking the application count button for a job listing expands an "Applications (N)" list; newly submitted application ("Test Applicant") to Marketing Manager job correctly appeared with count updated from 0 to 1, and Total Applications stat updated from 3 to 4.

Applications list per job shows distinct applicant name, email, phone (when provided), submission date, and message, clearly distinguishing between different job seekers (e.g. "Alex Johnson" vs "Maria Garcia" for Senior Frontend Developer; "Test Applicant" for Marketing Manager).

Created "QA Automation Engineer" job with Title, Industry (Technology), Employment Type (Full-time), Location (Remote), Min/Max Salary (90k-120k), Description, and skill (Selenium). Got "Job posted successfully!" toast and job appeared correctly in dashboard listing.

issue: No edit functionality for published jobs
actual: Delete works correctly (confirmation dialog, then job removed and Active Jobs count decremented from 6 to 5). However, each job card on the employer dashboard only exposes two controls: a "view applications" (users icon) button and a "delete" (trash icon) button — there is no edit/pencil icon, no edit link, and clicking the job title does not navigate to an edit form. Inspecting all dashboard buttons via DOM confirmed only "lucide-users" and "lucide-trash2" icons exist; no edit capability is present anywhere in the app.

issue: No access control preventing job seekers from posting jobs
actual: The application has no authentication/login system distinguishing employers from job seekers. The "Post a Job" link is visible and freely clickable in the main navigation bar on every page (homepage, job listing pages, etc.) for any anonymous visitor, and navigating to /employer/post-job succeeds without any credential check. Any job seeker can therefore create job postings exactly like an employer, as demonstrated earlier when FT-1 was tested without any login step.
